findings.statement: The exit criterion 'moves from a ready contract to verified implementation without redefining the requirement' names no artifact. Nothing says what a reviewer inspects to decide the requirement was not redefined, so two reviewers can judge the same run differently. A decidable form exists in this repository already: the sha256 of each contract input file still equals the hash dor.json recorded before the run.

The ticket does not settle whether /implement is SKILL.md text only or also ships code (a coverage report, a contract-immutability check, a new amigos subcommand). That decision changes what can be judged from outside: prompt-only delivery leaves every scenario here to review rather than to a test.

findings.target_section: Scenario: A readiness verdict recorded in the story is not trusted on its own
findings.statement: README section 14 says dor.json 'must contain ready: true' before business code changes; README section 18 says a committed dor.json is a record and never an authority because it is writable by the agent being gated. Two careful readers get two different preconditions for /implement, and one of them lets an agent authorise itself by editing a file.

findings.target_section: Scenario: A test for absent behaviour fails before the source changes
findings.statement: 'Establish a baseline where useful' gives no rule for when a baseline is required. The case it exists for is exactly the case an agent will judge as not useful: a test written after the code, which passes on the first run and therefore proves nothing about intent.

findings.target_section: Scenario: A Then no test can observe is named rather than dropped
findings.statement: 'Translate relevant Then clauses into tests' defines neither 'relevant' nor what happens to a Then no test in this repository can observe. STORY-005's contract contains such clauses ('no agent's prompt contains another agent's output'), so the first dogfooding target already carries the failure mode: silently skip the hard clauses and report the contract as verified.

'Check for scope expansion' names no basis of comparison. Candidates in this system are the acceptance scenarios, the 'Relevant Components' list in constraints.md, and the story's Out of Scope entries; the ticket picks none, so the check has no pass or fail.

'The implementation skill must not modify acceptance criteria' has no mechanical backing at v0.5: .amigos/** is exempt in .amigos/config.json, so the repository gate and the PreToolUse hook both permit an implementation agent to edit acceptance.feature. The only observable trace of a violation is hash drift against dor.json's contract_hash, and nothing currently compares them after a run.

Every governed edit /implement makes is subject to the gate's active-story resolution (AMIGOS_STORY, .amigos/ACTIVE, branch name). The ticket does not say that /implement makes its story resolvable. This checkout is currently on a detached HEAD, where branch resolution yields nothing and the first Write is refused.

findings.target_section: Scenario: The run takes no privileged path around the gate
findings.statement: The ticket lists no prohibition on the obvious escapes from a refusal: editing .claude/settings.json, uninstalling the pre-commit hook, or committing with --no-verify. README section 31 forbids a privileged path, but a skill that is never told this will find the escape faster than the fix.

findings.target_section: Scenario: An unsatisfied scenario is reported rather than made green
findings.statement: The ticket has no failure mode for a run that cannot finish: tests still failing, a behaviour that turns out to be infeasible, budget exhausted. Nothing says whether partial code stays, whether the run reports success, or what state.json declares. The v0.4 notes record a run terminated by a session rate limit, so this is not hypothetical.

On a contract conflict the ticket shows '/implement -> contract_change -> /amigos' without saying who acts. Both readings are buildable: /implement runs 'amigos state --set contract_change' and stops for a human, or it invokes /amigos itself. The second lets one session both discover a conflict and rewrite the criterion it conflicted with.

'Run tests and evals' names evals, which do not exist in this repository; eval export is phase 7 (v0.7) and 'amigos export-evals' is listed as a potential later command. The clause cannot be satisfied as written at v0.5, and an agent told to run evals will either invent one or quietly drop the step.

findings.target_section: Scenario: A ready contract reaches verified implementation
findings.statement: The ticket names no output for a run. Everything a reviewer would check afterwards - which scenario each test covers, which files changed and why, which scenarios remain unsatisfied - is only observable if the run leaves a report, and the ticket neither requires one nor says where it goes. /amigos settled the equivalent question by naming .amigos/runs/ as evidence outside the story directory.

v0.5 is judged by running /implement on Amigos Skills itself, and the v0.4 implementation notes record two environment facts that break that self-run: an agent type created in a session is not addressable in that session, and an edited SKILL.md serves its pre-edit text until something re-registers it. A milestone whose evidence is a self-run inherits both.
